summary: Discovery focused on model selection for multi-lingual, long-context generation with tool-calling. Customer leaning toward private/dedicated for data residency and latency but wants hosted economics comparison. Key concerns: context length support, function/tool calling, multilingual quality, and cost/latency tradeoffs.
transcript:
[00:00] Jesse Martin (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, really quick intros. I'm Jesse from Redwood, AE. Priya's our SE and Omar's on for infra questions.
[00:08] Liam Chen (Cascade): Hi all — Liam here, CTO. Marta's our ML lead, Samir infra, Anya product.
[00:13] Priya Shah (Redwood SE): Great, thanks. The goal today is to understand your workloads — model behaviors, context windows, multilingual needs, and any tool-calling you'd need. We'll talk hosted/dedicated/private tradeoffs and propose pilot next steps.
[00:30] Marta Ruiz (Cascade): Perfect. High level: we're building a customer-interaction summarization + action extraction pipeline. It needs to (a) handle long transcripts up to ~25k tokens, (b) call external tools/APIs to open tickets and classify risk, and (c) support English, Spanish, Portuguese and occasional Japanese. Latency target is sub-500ms token latency for interactive flows, batch can be higher.
[00:52] Samir Patel (Cascade Infra): Also important: data residency in EU for some customers, SOC2 compliance, and we'd prefer a VPC/private option for sensitive data. Cost is also a concern — we can't burn a ton of tokens.
[01:05] Jesse Martin (Redwood): Makes sense. Quick qual: current stack?
[01:09] Liam Chen: Mostly AWS, some on-prem for regulated clients. We use Kafka for event streaming, Postgres for state. No heavy GPU infra in-house other than dev boxes.
[01:18] Priya Shah: Thanks. For models, you mentioned long context and tool-calling. Are you evaluating open models or leaning toward managed closed models? Any constraints like model auditability?
[01:27] Marta Ruiz: We prefer open models for reproducibility and cost. We looked at LLaMA-3 family, Mistral large, and a couple of 70B/open checkpoints. We also tried Anthropic and OpenAI for baseline quality. Auditability is big — we need logs and deterministic model versions for later audits.
[01:43] Omar Reyes (Redwood): Got it. Two things where Redwood helps: we provide a model catalog with verified performance profiles (we can show empirical latency and token cost for 32k/64k runs), and the platform supports tool-calling (function calling) and structured output. For private deployments, the control plane can be customer-managed with KMS/HSM integration for keys.
[01:58] Anya Volk (Cascade Product): When you say tool-calling, can Redwood handle server-side function calls that our product triggers? We need the model to return structured JSON for the ticket API and also a call to our internal webhook.
[02:09] Priya Shah: Yes — we expose function/tool calling with typed schemas. On hosted, we mediate function calls securely, on Dedicated/Private you can run the tool-caller inside your network. There can be slight latency differences depending on routing.
[02:22] Marta Ruiz: How about context lengths — we might expand later to 64k. Which open models do you recommend? We've seen big quality drop for some weight-quantized checkpoints at high context.
[02:31] Priya Shah: Right. For high-context, Mistral M3-32k variants and LLaMA-3-32k/64k checkpoints usually do well. We also have Redwood-verified quantized variants that preserve quality at 32k; 64k is model-dependent. We typically recommend a two-tier approach: use a 32k variant for interactive flows and stitch longer context with summarization / KV-cache prefixing for very long docs. For customers wanting full 64k native, we can run 64k-optimized instances (different kernel selection, memory config) on Dedicated or Private.
[03:03] Samir Patel: Does 64k run require different hardware? We're thinking about Dedicated with reserved GPUs.
[03:07] Omar Reyes: Yes — 64k can require more GPU memory; we often recommend A100 80GB or the newer H100 80/96GB class for native 64k without aggressive quantization. On Redwood Dedicated we can provide instance types and a sizing estimate. For Private on-prem, you'll need similar capacity; we can help with sizing.
[03:29] Liam Chen: On multilingual — we've noticed some models are skewed to English. Which models maintain parity across Spanish/Portuguese/Japanese?
[03:36] Priya Shah: Mistral M3 family has strong multi-lingual ability; LLaMA-3 improved but sometimes needs instruction finetune for non-English. We recommend running a small eval set (5-10 examples per language) as part of the pilot. We'll run Redwood's quality monitor to flag regressions and map tokens to cost per language.
[03:54] Marta Ruiz: OK — about tool-calling reliability. If the model hallucinates the JSON schema or misformats the API call, how do you help with that?
[04:02] Priya Shah: We provide structured parsing tooling: either strict function calling (schema-enforced) or post-parse validation hooks. For mission-critical flows you can run the call in a sandbox and only commit after validation. Also, Redwood Optimize can suggest prompt/layouts and quantization profiles that reduce hallucinations.
[04:20] Anya Volk: Do you have customers running hybrid routing — e.g., hosted for low-volume, dedicated for high-volume or private for regulated customers?
[04:26] Jesse Martin: Absolutely. Smart routing can route by customer tier, region, or latency SLO. If a request hits a regulated tenant it goes to Private/Dedicated; if capacity constrained, we can fall back to a smaller hosted model. That routing is policy-driven and is part of the Redwood Console.
[04:41] Samir Patel: Security specifics: KMS, audit logs, RBAC, SSO?
[04:45] Jesse Martin: We support customer-managed KMS, detailed request-level audit logs, SSO/SAML, and RBAC for console and API keys. We'll attach SOC2 and our security pack in the follow-up.
[04:57] Liam Chen: Cost: give us a sense — how different is cost between hosted and Dedicated for our workload (~300k tokens/day, spike to 1M)?
[05:05] Jesse Martin: Basic rule: hosted is pay-as-you-go with per-token pricing; Dedicated gives lower unit cost if you commit reserved capacity. We'll send an example math sheet — for your 300k baseline Dedicated typically breaks even if you sustain high utilization; spikes can be covered with burst capacity.
[05:19] Marta Ruiz: For the pilot, we'd like to compare a few model variants: Mistral-32k quantized, LLaMA-3-32k, and a smaller 7B for cost/latency baseline. Can Redwood host the models for benchmarking?
[05:29] Priya Shah: Yes — we can run a 2-week pilot with those variants on either Hosted or a Dedicated pilot pool. We'll run latency and quality evals across your prompt set and give you token cost and throughput numbers.
[05:40] Omar Reyes: Quick note on deployment: if you go Private, the control plane can be centralized but compute lives in your VPC. That gives you auditability and data residency. It also means upgrades follow your maintenance windows.
[05:53] Samir Patel: Any gotchas with KV cache / prefixing when stitching conversations? We've seen context leakage across sessions on other infra.
[05:59] Priya Shah: We namespace KV caches per conversation and customer; Redwood's runtime enforces isolation and has TTLs. We'll also set up tracing to surface any cache hits/misses in the Console.
[06:11] Marta Ruiz: About hallucination on tool results — sometimes the model generates an action that contradicts the API response. Is there a recommended pattern?
[06:18] Priya Shah: Pattern is: validate API responses server-side before committing state, use function calling with strict schemas, and prefer two-step confirmation for high risk actions. Redwood Optimize can surface examples where hallucination rates are high for certain prompts.
[06:33] Anya Volk: For function calling, do you support streaming intermediate generator tokens and then a final function call? We need progressive UI updates.
[06:40] Priya Shah: Yes — streaming with function-calling metadata is supported. You can stream tokens and then receive the structured function payload at the end, or use turn-based structured outputs. Streaming latency will depend on network and chosen model.
[06:53] Liam Chen: If we want to keep everything EU-resident, can we run a Private control plane in our EU VPC with Redwood support?
[06:59] Jesse Martin: Yes. Our Private option supports customer-managed networking in-region. We'll document the onboarding steps; it usually takes 4-8 weeks depending on infra readiness.
[07:10] Marta Ruiz: Timeline — we need a pilot in May to validate model choice by end of Q2. Is that feasible?
[07:15] Jesse Martin: Totally feasible. Proposed: sign a short pilot agreement, Redwood provisions a Dedicated pilot pool or Hosted pilot nodes with your chosen model variants, we run the 2-week benchmarks and then review.
[07:25] Samir Patel: For Dedicated sizing, can you recommend GPU counts? We have to budget.
[07:29] Omar Reyes: We'll produce a sizing doc. For 32k interactive with ~500ms token latency at 300k tokens/day, estimated starting point is 2-4 A100 80GB (shared) with autoscale. For 64k native, plan for more headroom — 4-8 GPUs depending on concurrency. We will provide more exact numbers after we run the sample traces.
[07:46] Marta Ruiz: Anything else?
[07:49] Priya Shah: We'll include suggested prompt engineering guardrails for multilingual prompts and an eval harness to compare per-language quality. Also a recommended quantization profile that balances cost and quality.
[07:58] Jesse Martin: Great. Recap and actions: we'll send security docs + pricing matrix, Priya will set up the technical deep dive, Marta sends sample prompts, and we'll schedule pilot kickoff.
[08:10] Liam Chen: Thanks all, looks good.
[08:12] Jesse Martin: Thanks everyone, talk soon.
[08:15] (call ends)
